I checked the quote against the page and read it against all four parts of the rule. I'm calling it **borderline**. Parts 1, 2 and 4 pass. Part 3 depends on how "the next couple of months" is read, and the rule doesn't settle that.

**The page.** The page opened. It is a full third-party transcript of the Google I/O 2018 developer keynote on singjupost.com. It says the event took place on Tuesday, May 8, 2018 at Shoreline Amphitheatre, and it lists Pichai as CEO of Google. The quoted words are there exactly: "All these features are going to be rolling out to Google Photos users in the next couple of months." They come at the end of Pichai's Google Photos section, just after the colourising of black-and-white photos and just before he moves on to the Tensor Processing Units (Google's AI chips). This is a transcript, not a news report, so it is a primary source.

**The four parts:**
1. **Role: passes.** On 2018-05-08 Pichai was chief executive of Google, which he had been since 2015-10-02.
2. **Forward-looking and about AI: passes.** He introduces Google Photos as a product "built from the ground up using AI." The features (suggested actions, brightness fixes, turning a photographed document into a PDF, colourising old photos) are AI features, and the words are about rolling them out to users. That fits the rule's allowance for an AI product shipping. It is a similar kind of claim to the recorded 2023 Magic Editor one.
3. **A date or length of time: borderline.** "The next couple of months" doesn't say how many months.
   - Reading 3 says "a few years" names no length.
   - The ledger has also applied that reading to "the next few months" and "the coming months." That application was the agent's, and it is flagged for your ruling.
   - "A couple" can mean exactly two, which would give a due date of 2018-07-08, or it can mean "a few", which would leave the claim undated. Neither ruled reading covers it, so I'm not choosing one.
4. **Primary source: passes.** A transcript counts.

**Already recorded?** No. The only recorded claim from this keynote is the John Legend voice one ("later this year"), and that is a different claim.
